newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Delta eyes 400,000 oz gold a year by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Delta eyes 400,000 oz gold a year by 2000.

text.p: Delta Gold NL said on Wednesday planned new mine projects could nearly double its annual gold output to 400,000 ounces a year by 2000.

A 50/50 joint venture project with Metex Resources NL at Beasley Creek in Western Australia would provide a 150,000 ounce resource with a further 40,000 ounces indicated in a surrounding prospect, chief operating officer Terry Burgess told the Diggers and Dealers mining conference here.
Burgess said Delta has also purchased a 100 percent interest in three gold properties in Zimbabwe.
"These properties are in the Kwe Kwe area near the Chaka prospect at the heart of the Midlands gold belt, the most productive in Zimbabwe," Burgess said.

Delta earlier on Wednesday said it produced a record 226,589 ounces of gold in 1996/97 (July/June), underpinned by its 50 percent owned Kanowna Belle mine in Western Australia, Burgess said. North Ltd owns the other half of Kanowna Belle.
Delta's 40 percent-owned Granny Smith mine, also in Western Australia, was producing at record levels. The mine is 60 percent owned by Placer Dome Inc.
Production from Delta's 33 percent-owned Hartley platinum mine in Zimbabwe should start by the end of September and reach full capacity output of 180,000 ounces a year by the end of 1998.
The remaining 67 prcent of the Hartley mine is owned by The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd.
Delta earlier on Monday said it was putting its proposed Golden Feather mine project on hold because of low world gold prices.
